name: StreamVerse AI Anomaly Intelligence
tag: Watches your live data streams and flags unusual patterns early, so you fix problems before customers notice.

scenarios.title: Catch a checkout slowdown
scenarios.ask: Watch our checkout stream at {eps} events per second and tell us when something looks wrong.

inputs.label: Days of history to learn from

steps: Baseline
Learned normal patterns from {history} of data, including the lunch and evening peaks.
Watcher
Response time on the payment step rose to {=round(380 + 40 * sensitivity)} ms, about 2.4 times normal for 2:10 PM.
Correlator
Lined it up with a deploy 6 minutes earlier and a rise in retries from one payment region.
Notifier
Sent one alert to the on-call engineer with the chart, the deploy and a suggested rollback.

result.title: Anomaly flagged
rows: Deploy plus one slow payment region

followups: Why not just use fixed thresholds?
Fixed limits either fire every lunchtime peak or miss a slowdown at 3 AM. StreamVerse compares each moment with what's normal for that time and day.
Sharper settings alert sooner but send more alerts you'll dismiss. Most teams start on Balanced and adjust after two weeks.
Does it fix things on its own?
Not by default. It suggests an action, and you can allow simple, reversible actions such as a rollback later.

scenarios.title: Sensor fleet drift
scenarios.ask: We stream readings from {sensors} temperature sensors in cold storage. Find any that are drifting.
steps: Ingest
Took in {=round(sensors * 86400 / interval)} readings over the last day.
Watcher
Found {=max(1, round(sensors * 0.015))} sensors reading slowly higher than their neighbors for 5 days.
Classifier
Marked them as likely sensor drift, not a real temperature rise, because nearby sensors stayed flat.
Notifier
Opened a maintenance ticket with the sensor IDs and their locations on the floor plan.
followups: How does it tell drift from a real problem?
A real problem shows up across nearby sensors at once. A single sensor creeping away from its neighbors usually points to the sensor itself.
Can it watch other data too?
Yes. Any steady stream works, such as orders, logins, machine readings or queue lengths.

scenarios.title: Cut alert noise
scenarios.ask: Our team gets {alerts} alerts a day and ignores most of them. Clean this up.
steps: Auditor
Read 30 days of alerts. {=round(alerts * 0.62)} a day closed with no action.
Grouper
Combined repeats from the same cause into one incident.
Tuner
Replaced 18 fixed thresholds with learned baselines.
Router
Sent each alert type to the team that owns it instead of everyone.
followups: The new rules were replayed against 30 days of history before switching on. You review that replay before anything changes.
A first pass takes about a week of learning, then it keeps adjusting as your traffic changes.
